components.name: PostgreSQL source of truth (posts, graph) - 2 shards

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: db.r6g.large — AWS RDS PostgreSQL us-east-1 / On-Demand / Single-AZ (band high = Multi-AZ) / 730 h per month; INSTANCE-HOURS ONLY (excludes storage, provisioned IOPS and backup above the free allocation). Band: deployment spread: low = Single-AZ, high = Multi-AZ. Both are on-demand, standard-tier, us-east-1 PostgreSQL, so the band is fully in scope. Multi-AZ is ~2x Single-AZ.

citations.note: $0.225/h Single-AZ x 730 = 16425c/month. MySQL/MariaDB run ~3.9% cheaper than PostgreSQL for the same class.

assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 25,000 req/s peak. Mix: 72% feed reads, 18% publish, 8% engagement events, 2% archive/analytics reads

assumptions.subject: builder
assumptions.statement: The materialiser is the constraint. Post events fan out to ~150 follower feeds each; engagement events are 1:1 counter updates. Blended, an instance clears ~900 events/s. The fanout amplification is encoded in that CAPACITY, not as a visit probability above 1, so arrivals stay literal request counts

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: Feed reads are 100% cache-served by design (that is the point of materialising); 8% miss to the source of truth for backfill after an eviction or a cold user

assumptions.subject: db
assumptions.statement: The source of truth is 2 SHARDS - two instances that each take half the writes. Unlike a Multi-AZ standby, a shard really does add capacity, so modelling it as instances=2 is honest. Each shard is still a single writer with no modelled standby

assumptions.subject: q
assumptions.statement: The event bus runs 3 brokers for quorum. At ~6,500 msg/s it is ~7% loaded; brokers here are an availability choice, not a throughput one

assumptions.subject: gw
assumptions.statement: COST WARNING: at ~21.6 billion requests/month a per-request API gateway is ~$64,800/month - about 20x the entire compute fleet. That is the honest consequence of putting a managed gateway in front of a 25k-rps read path. An ALB plus in-app auth is materially cheaper and is the first thing to challenge in this design

assumptions.subject: pricing
assumptions.statement: Monthly usage volumes (egress/storage/requests) are derived from AVERAGE load = peak / 3; capacity and instance counts are sized to PEAK. A single system_rps cannot carry both, so the peak:average ratio is stated here rather than hidden in a volume.

assumptions.subject: engine
assumptions.statement: The engine models steady-state arrivals, not backlog. A consumer running below capacity is shown as healthy; it does NOT model queue-depth growth, consumer lag, or the recovery time after a partition outage. Those are the failure modes that actually hurt an event-driven feed and they are out of scope here

assumptions.subject: scope
assumptions.statement: Ranking/ML scoring, notifications and the moderation pipeline are OUT of this reference. The feed is chronological-with-materialisation

_library.summary: Event-driven feed where writes publish to a bus and stream workers materialise per-user feeds.
